title: Terrel Bernard Met With The Media After OTAs | Buffalo Bills
text: a lot of injuries, a lot of things, you know, kind of getting banged up throughout the year. Um, trying to fight through it and still, you know, persevere and be who I am. Um, but it was it was tough physically and mentally. Um, so kind of get away uh for a little bit in the offseason and, you know, reset and, you know, try to get my body back and get as healthy as possible. Um, but it's been fun to be be back around back around the guys and, you know, try to try to lead. Is there a balance between playing hard for or hurt for your teammates when you're injured and trying to stay out on the field and trying to take care of yourself, meaning like, you know, where you can't be the guy that people have seen you be on the field? >> Yeah, I think it it's a it's a it's a fine line. Um, and you know, I think for me personally, I've grown up a certain way and, you know, kind of came under a certain brand of if I'm able to go, I'm going to go. Um, and you know, honestly realizing now that's not always, you know, the the best case scenario for the team and for myself too. Um, so that's a a learning area for me. Um, as I as I kind of navigated last year a little bit. Um, but yeah, to answer your question, I think I think there's a there's a fine line and you know, I think the longer you're in the league, you kind of figure out your body, you figure out what you can and can't do and you know, what's productive for the team. >> Linebacker, you play, you hit people, you run to the ball. But are there things about this defense that might even suit you better or you're encouraged about or something like that? >> Yeah, I think so. Um, you know, going and having meetings with Jim and, you know, talking to eggs and stuff, I think there's certain things that that, you know, fit my play style and, you know, things that I'm good at which I'm excited about. um you know you it's like you said at the end of the day it's it's football and the position is the position but you know I feel like there's certain things that um you know I'll be able to you know play within within my game and you know execute a little bit >> what are the differences what are the differences in what you will be doing what you can be doing in this compared to the previous >> uh yeah it's it's tough to say right now I think you know right now we're just kind of going through basic installs and um that type of stuff but I think you know just the aspect of blitzing um the aspect of, you know, being in coverage and, you know, having a guy and staying on a guy, um, and being able to kind of float to the ball. I think, you know, those are things that I've I've been good at in the past and something that I look to improve on and, you know, really try to take another step in in this defense. >> So, you're seeing there's going to be more of that in this defense. You know, we look at it and we see you moving over a few feet, right, is basically what you're doing. But, you're saying there's going to be different responsibilities than you had in the previous defense. >> Yeah, I think so. anytime you have a new scheme, a new system, there's going to be different um responsibilities and and techniques and things that you want to do and things that they want to see you do. Um so I think, you know, figuring that out um as you go through OTAAS, as you get through training camp into the into the preseason and the regular season, I think having that um that detail and you know, really understanding what they want to see out of us. Um I feel like that's, you know, where where we can improve. How much of a drag was last? Because I remember talking to you probably in November before you got hurt for the rest of the season and you at that point seemed like like you had had enough like you were really kind of down on the way gone. How much of a drag was that on you last year? >> Yeah, it was tough. It was probably my hardest year as a as a football player to be honest. Um like you said, man, just just battling through injuries. Um you know, not feeling like myself for a lot of the year trying to come back and then you know, having something else pop up. Uh, so it was tough. You know, I tried to, you know, do the best that I could to to still be a leader and still be out in front and still, you know, be who I am. Um, but it does take a toll on you. And, you know, it was it was it was a tough year for me, but, you know, I'm I'm trying to flush it and honestly, you know, move on and try to get my body in a position to where I can be effective and and go out there and play good football. >> Obviously, no Matt anymore next to a guy you're used to playing with, but there is a competition and you have Dorian who's returning, Caleb Elam or Elam Morris. What have you seen from him? How excited are you to see these guys compete to play next to you? >> Yeah. No, it's been fun. Um, I feel like all the young guys have come in and and, you know, really took a step um, you know, from the first day just learning the installs to now coming out here and trying to compete and, you know, playing against, you know, a really good offense obviously. Um, it's been fun though. I think, you know, I'm doing my part and trying to help those guys and those guys are doing their part and learning the system and learning, you know, what what's expected of them. Um, so it's been it's been a good a good time so far. What is it like for you at this point in your career to have all of this changed for the first time? New coordinator, a different head coach even though you know him, different scheme. What is it like kind of having a reset at this stage of your career? >> Yeah, I mean it's it's football, man, at the end of the day. Um like you said, it's new it's a new system. Um a new era of Bills football. Um but you know, I think all the guys are excited. You know, we all know Joe and you know, who he is and what he brings to the table and what he expects out of us. Um, so I think, you know, looking at it from that aspect, it's it's exciting. You know, you get a a fresh start, you get a new a new playbook, new coaches, new everything. Um, so it's it's exciting, though. >> How are you physically? >> How are you now? >> Uh, you seem good, right? >> Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. No, I'm I'm still rehabbing. Um, you know, I had a had a little thing at the end of the season that I had to get cleaned up. Um, but moving on from that, you know, I'm I'm uh you know, feeling feeling better. Um, taking it day by day, man. trying to get get everything back to to baseline to where I feel feel 100%. >> What have been your impressions of Jim Leonard? >> Sorry, one more time. >> Yeah, Jim's a cool dude. Um, obviously played in the league for a long time. Um, and you can tell he's he's been around the game for a really long time. He knows the game in and out and I feel like he um, you know, sees things from a player and a coach's perspective, which is which is really cool. Um, you know, he's a he's a really really smart guy. He's been fun to just hang out and talk ball with. um get out here on the field and you know really trying to learn new things from him. Um but yeah, he's been he's been great. >> TV, sorry if you were asked, but what what have your impressions of Joe as the head coach now? Ben, I obviously knew him. >> Yeah. Yeah. No, it's been it's been great. Um like I said, I told those guys, you know, we all knew Joe before. Um so to, you know, really see him, you know, step into that role and become, you know, the guy, the head coach, uh it's been it's been fun. his energy, you know, his passion for the game and what he expects out of us is is, you know, evident just so far in the the meetings that we've had. So, I'm I'm excited. >> I know it's early, but what were the things that stand out to you about this defense in terms of the, you know, this the scheme and the way you guys are going to play? >> I think just the the opportunity to be multiple. You know, we got a bunch of different um fronts, a bunch of different personnels that we can use. Um, and you know, I feel like they try to get guys active. You know, whether that's a outside linebacker, an inside linebacker, a safety, a nickel. Um, you know, I feel like it's been, you know, a little bit of everything right now. You get to, you know, kind of see where where it's going to evolve to and, you know, what what the featured, uh, pieces are going to be. So, it's been it's been fun.

title: DeWayne Carter Talks With The Media After Practice | Buffalo Bills
text: Landen is also a guy that was in your shoes early on. He got hurt obviously. We saw him a lot bigger out here and coach said he I'm sorry, maybe Joe or Brandon said a lot bigger. What's it been like going through the battle with him to get back? Yeah, he's my guy. You know, one of the silver linings about being hurt alongside somebody is you get really close. We had similar schedules with rehab and working out and that's really what we did, right? It's kind of you make a decision, you can either soak and sit there and feel sorry for yourself or make a decision, right? How can I get better and what aspects can I get better? So we chose fitness as an outlet, right? So we became really close and it's been cool to see him and how good he looks. What are your initial impressions of Jim Leonard? I love coach Leonard. I really do. He brings us a lot of energy and juice to the game. You can tell he was, you know, he's played the game before too. So it's always funny when you see pictures of him pop up every once in a while in his playing days, but he's a really smart coach about coaching. He he loves the game. I think it's been really awesome. What do you think of your new upbeat guy? Was it tough though mentally at times going through everything that you went through with the health? Yeah, 100%. I mean it's it's definitely kind of like I talked about it a little bit earlier. It's just you make a decision. I mean I think so my first felt sorry for myself about maybe two or three days, right? That soaking period and then after your your surgery I'm back in the building around the guys, it's hard to be negative, you know? Cuz that's why I say like obviously game was taken away, but there's a lot worse places in life that I could be instead of hurt in an NFL facility, right? So that's kind of be the mindset. How much are you weighing these days and what are some of the expectations you're setting for yourself this year? Yeah, so I'm anywhere between 325 to 330. I'm expecting myself to play around 320, 325. And then expectation overall, I mean I don't really have any. I just take it day by day and obviously there's different goals and stuff I have in my head and with my coaches, but at the end of day I'm taking it day by day. I know you didn't cross over with him at Duke, but how cool is it to have Bruno Fina out here, another Duke guy? It's awesome. It's been really cool cuz I got to know his dad a lot throughout my first two years here. It's fun to come out. I'm really excited for him. He's a good young player. And obviously you know, help my Blue Devils get ACC championship, man. So we got a lot of a lot of love for the guy.

title: Atlanta Falcons Head Coach Kevin Stefanski OTA Media Availability | May 19, 2026 | Press Conference
text: OTAA number two today. Uh really pleased with where the guys are. They're working very hard with a lot of work yet to be done, but excited to be out there. Uh but really the focus as we do those seven on sevens, those teams, the focus still remains fundamentals and techniques. But really happy with the the effort that that the guys are uh displaying out there on the field in the wait room in the meeting room. Really a team that is working very very hard and I appreciate that. Uh now with that he's able to do more and more football uh at the direction of our medical staff. Uh so we've been working handinhand with what that looks like. Uh but that time is coming. >> How do you plan to put snaps at? >> Uh very intentionally. Uh I think it's uh our job. I think Tommy Reese does an outstanding job of making sure that we're uh intentional about how we want this to operate. And uh you know, one guy will be up first one period and then switch the next period and and and rotate every single day and and really almost every drill because uh the truth is we're trying to get the the best version of all of our players. So, we want to mix and match guys in in different spots. >> What do you want from a QB like right now? Like for you in a month from now to say, "Hey, he had a really good month." What does it look like? I think for the quarterback room in particular, it's grasping our system. Uh taking the lead of of of that or in that regard and then uh going and operating at a high level in these practices. Uh as you guys well know, seven on seven is an offensive drill. There's no pass rush out there. So you'll see our offensive line out there so that they feel players around them. Uh but it's really a passing drill that that is skews the advantage to the offense. So, we want our guys to operate well in those periods and and uh you know, pitch and catch with with at at a good clip and then in the team periods and everything else we're doing, just having a very good command of what we're doing and why we're doing it. >> To that point, what are kind of some markers or checkpoints that that you see from guys out on the field that show you that they are absorbing kind of the install of what y'all are doing? >> It's a good question. That being said, there are mistakes and and that's okay. This is the time of the year where you're going to make a mistake and then we're going to learn from it. We're going to identify the reasons that it was made and we're going to correct them. So, I think the you're seeing from the certainly the veterans that have been around um you're seeing them continue, God bless you, seeing them continue to get better in each rep, get better in each practice. The younger players, the rookies, less time on task, if you will. So, uh they're our job as coaches is to get them up to speed ASAP. And, uh I think the rookies have really understood that and they're going to learn at their own pace as well. as you go about kind of evaluating the quarterback competition, are there individual things you're looking from for each guy differently or is it more about the unit and the team? >> It's a good question. I think as coaches, as position coaches, you know, you want your room, your position to perform well and and you certainly look at it globally in that regard. Uh also for us as coaches and us as teachers, we want to focus on each individual player and and all of our players are in different uh points of their career and and are dealing with maybe it's dealing with injury or dealing with a new system or or whatever it might be. So uh that's the the part of the challenge for us as coaches is getting the best version of our players. So uh there's not a number of hey we need you to be this percentage in a drill. So, you don't want to get too in in into the weeds of of changing releases and those type of things. Having said that, there are uh subtle quarter turn adjustments that I think you can make with technique. And that may be it may be where the toe is pointed when the ball is thrown. It may be how you're transferring your your weight from your back foot. It may be how how you finish your your throw. So, I think it's all of the above. You know, I equate a lot of times to golf and and swing thoughts. You know, I can't you can't give too many swing thoughts and now you have nothing. you're not really focused on anything. But, uh, with quarterbacks, by and large, once they're at our level, we're making them the most efficient, uh, that they can be with their current, uh, mechanics, if you will. >> With Mike's recovery, are you at a point now where you feel like that the time you can narrow a timet down to wanting him to be at a certain point, at a certain date? Is the goal for him to be a full participant? >> Yeah, you know, I'm really that's not really where we are thinking at this point. really focused on uh OTAA number two and and of course we've looked at the calendar, we've talked about those things, but uh definitely as a staff, definitely for Mike, we kind of have the blinders on and and are really just looking at what's in front of us. >> It's no secret that when you were in Cleveland, you dealt with a lot of quarterback adversity. Uh but our our job as coaches is to find a way to win on Sundays with our players and maximize the talents of our individual players. Obviously, the quarterback position goes to the forefront of those discussions. Uh but for myself, for coach Vanpel, for coach Ree, uh the the idea here is is to keep a narrow focus and and worry about what's in front of us. Uh and if you have these if you have that mentality, I do believe that individually and collectively, you can get a little bit better every single day. And then, uh those type of uh speaking quarterback wise, those type of decisions that you have to make, those are down the road. But we don't want to keep our focus there. We want to really be where our feet are, if you will. point that when when you're in the meeting room with Michael to uh who's kind of I know that ABP is kind of like their their guy, but >> are you in those meetings? Is is Tanner in there? Tommy, like how do you make sure that it's, as you said before, it's one voice talking to those guys? I >> I do think Tori, it's a good question. Uh Trevor Simeon, Tua, Mike, Jack Strand. Uh you know, it's fun with having uh you know, Trevor in there now.
